'''Philip H. Bucksbaum''' (born January 14, 1953, in [[Grinnell, Iowa]]) is an [[Americans|American]] [[atomic physicist]], the Marguerite Blake Wilbur Professor in Natural Science in the Departments of Physics, Applied Physics, and Photon Science at [[Stanford University]] and the [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite book|title=Marquis Who's Who in America, 62nd Edition|year=2008|publisher=Marquis Publishing|location=New Providence, NJ}}</ref>  He also directs the [[Stanford PULSE Institute]].

He is a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] and a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], the [[American Physical Society]], and the [[Optical Society]], and was elected [[Optical Society#OSA presidents|President of the Optical Society for 2014]].<ref>{{cite news|title=SLAC's Phil Bucksbaum elected VP of Optical Society|url=http://news.stanford.edu/thedish/?p=15349|access-date=16 June 2013|newspaper=The Dish|date=20 October 2011}}</ref><ref name=LaserFocusArticls>{{cite news|last=Mather|first=Lee|title=OSA elects Philip H. Bucksbaum as 2012 vice president|url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/articles/oiq/2011/10/osa-elects-bucksbaum-as-2012-vice-president.html|access-date=2013-06-14|newspaper=Laser Focus World|date=2011-10-19}}</ref> He develops and uses  ultrafast strong field lasers to study fundamental atomic and [[molecular]] interactions, particularly  [[coherent control]] of the quantum dynamics of electrons, atoms, and molecules using coherent radiation pulses from the far-infrared to hard x-rays, with pulse durations from [[picoseconds]] to less than a [[femtosecond]]. In 2020, Bucksbaum received the [[Norman F. Ramsey Prize in Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics, and in Precision Tests of Fundamental Laws and Symmetries]] for his pioneering explorations of ultrafast strong field physics from the optical to the X-ray regime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-09-19 |title=Phil Bucksbaum to Receive American Physical Society's 2020 Norman F. Ramsey Prize {{!}} Physics Department |url=https://physics.stanford.edu/news/phil-bucksbaum-receive-american-physical-societys-2020-norman-f-ramsey-prize |access-date=2023-10-30 |website=physics.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref>

== Biography ==
=== Early life and education ===
Bucksbaum spent his early childhood in [[Grinnell, Iowa|Grinnell]], a small farming and college community in south-central Iowa.<ref name=Schoutens>{{cite book|last=Schouten|first=Katherine|title=At Home in the Heartland: A Bucksbaum Family Album|year=2007|publisher=History Works|location=Chicago}}</ref> He graduated as the class valedictorian from [[Washington High School (Cedar Rapids, Iowa)|Washington High School]] in [[Cedar Rapids]] in 1971.<ref name="WHS Graduation">{{cite news|title=Washington High to Graduate 481|newspaper=Cedar Rapids Gazette|date=June 10, 1971|page=10}}</ref> He received a bachelor's degree in Physics from [[Harvard College]] in 1975.<ref>{{cite book|title=Yearbook of Harvard and Radcliffe 1975 Number 339|year=1975|publisher=Harvard Yearbook Publications|location=Cambridge, MA}}</ref> Bucksbaum attended graduate school at the University of California at Berkeley, receiving his Ph.D. in 1980.<ref name=ACAP />

=== Professional career ===
Following a one-year postdoctoral appointment at [[Lawrence Berkeley Laboratory]], Bucksbaum joined [[Bell Telephone Laboratories]], where he remained until [[Columbia University]] appointed him Adjunct Associate Professor in Applied Physics in 1989.<ref>{{cite book|title=Department of Applied Physics, Columbia University|year=1989|publisher=Columbia University|location=New York, NY|page=14|url=https://apam.columbia.edu/files/seasdepts/applied-physics-and-applied-math/pdf-files/AP_Brochure_1989.pdf|editor=JoAnn Winston}}</ref>  In 1990 he moved to [[Ann Arbor, MI]] to accept a Professorship in Physics at the [[University of Michigan]]. He became Otto Laporte Collegiate Professor in Physics in 1997, and Peter Franken University Professor in 2005.<ref name=ACAP>{{cite web|title=Array of Contemporary American Physicists|url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?bucksbaump|publisher=American Institute of Physics|access-date=2013-06-15}}</ref>

Bucksbaum joined the faculty of Stanford in 2005, with joint appointments in Physics, Applied Physics, and Photon Science.<ref>{{cite news|title=Report of the President to the Board of Trustees|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2005/october12/prezreport-101205.html|access-date=16 June 2013|newspaper=Stanford News|date=12 October 2005}}</ref>  He was named to the Marguerite Blake Wilbur Chair in Natural Science at Stanford in 2009,<ref name="MBW Professor">{{cite news|title=Report of the President to the Board of Trustees|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2009/april15/president-report-trustees-041509.html|access-date=June 16, 2013|newspaper=Stanford News|date= April 15, 2009}}</ref> and currently directs the PULSE Institute at Stanford and SLAC.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bucksbaum appointed to direct Ultrafast Science Center|newspaper=Stanford News|date=18 October 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Gewin|first=Virginia|title=Movers: Philip Bucksbaum, director, Stanford Ultrafast Science Center, Stanford, California|journal=Nature|date=18 January 2006|volume=439|issue=7074|page=366|doi=10.1038/nj7074-366a|s2cid=109946661|doi-access=free}}</ref>

=== Research summary ===
Bucksbaum's graduate research at Berkeley was on the parity non-conserving neutral [[weak interaction]] in atomic [[thallium]].<ref>{{cite book|last=Commins|first=Eugene D.|title=Atomic Physics 7 |year=1981|publisher=Springer|location=New York|isbn=978-1-4615-9208-2|page=121|editor=Daniel Kleppner|doi=10.1007/978-1-4615-9206-8_5|chapter=Status of Experimental Searches for Parity Violation in Atoms}}</ref><ref>
[http://www.escholarship.org/uc/item/317960r4 Bucksbaum, P. H. ''Measurement of the Parity Non-conserving Neutral Weak Interaction in Atomic Thallium'' (Ph.D. Thesis, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory)]</ref> He co-authored a textbook on the larger subject of [[electroweak interaction]]s after completing his doctoral thesis.<ref>Commins, Eugene D., and Philip H. Bucksbaum. Weak Interactions of Leptons and Quarks. Cambridge: Cambridge Press, 1983; {{ISBN|0521273706}}</ref>

At [[Bell Laboratories]] he became interested in [[ultrafast]] and strong field laser-matter interactions. For a time, he co-held the record for the shortest wavelength coherent radiation produced in the laboratory.<ref name=35.5nmRecord>{{cite journal|last=Fischer|first=R|author2=M. Schubert|title=Trends in Nonlinear Optics|journal=Annalen der Physik|date=March 16, 2006|volume=498|issue=6–8|pages=455–471|doi=10.1002/andp.19864980608}}</ref>   He was one of the team that used similar methods to develop  the first ultrafast angle-resolved vuv photoemission methods.<ref name=Himpsel>{{cite journal|last=Himpsel|first=Franz J.|author2=Neville Smith|title=Photoelectron Spectroscopy|journal=Physics Today|year=1985|volume=38|issue=12|page=60|doi=10.1063/1.880997|bibcode=1985PhT....38l..60H}}</ref>
In 1985 he turned to the study of strong-field ionization of atoms. His early work on [[above threshold ionization]] of atoms established the role of [[ponderomotive force]]s in laser-electron interactions through studies of electron surfing in ultrafast laser pulses as well as the high-intensity [[Kapitsa–Dirac effect]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Nature Research Highlights: Making Light of the Matter|journal=Nature|date=2001-09-13|volume=413|issue=6852|pages=142–3|doi=10.1038/35093065|pmid=11557974 | last1 = Freimund | first1 = DL | last2 = Aflatooni | first2 = K | last3 = Batelaan | first3 = H|url=http://digitalcommons.unl.edu/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1130&context=physicsfacpub | bibcode=2001Natur.413..142F|s2cid=4351324|url-access=subscription}}</ref>  He also discovered and explained the mechanism of [[bond softening]] in strong-field molecular dissociation.<ref name="Bond Softening">{{cite journal|last=Sheehy|first=Brian|author2=Louis DiMauro|title=Atomic and Molecular Dynamics in Intense Optical Fields|journal=Annual Review of Physical Chemistry|date=October 1996|volume=47|pages=463–494|doi=10.1146/annurev.physchem.47.1.463|bibcode=1996ARPC...47..463S|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1235047}}</ref>
His pioneering development of broadband coherent [[THz radiation]] (so-called "half-cycle pulses")<ref>{{cite journal|last=Reimann|first=Klaus|title=Table-top sources of ultrashort THz pulses|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|date=10 October 2007|volume=70|issue=10|page=1587| doi=10.1088/0034-4885/70/10/r02 |bibcode=2007RPPh...70.1597R|s2cid=121223287 }}</ref> helped to advance the field of [[Terahertz time-domain spectroscopy|ultrafast THz spectroscopy]]. He has subsequently used ultrafast lasers to study problems in quantum sculpting,<ref name="QuantumSculpting in Sci Am">{{cite journal|last=Collins|first=Graham P.|title=News and Analysis: Quantum Sculpting|journal=Scientific American|date=May 1999|url=http://www.nature.com/scientificamerican/journal/v280/n5/pdf/scientificamerican0599-35.pdf|volume=280|issue=5|doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0599-35|doi-broken-date=July 12, 2025 }}</ref> quantum information,<ref>{{cite news |title=Newsbreak: Light stores and retrieves quantum information |url=https://www.laserfocusworld.com/articles/print/volume-36/issue-3/world-news/newsbreaks/newbreaks.html |access-date=2013-06-15|newspaper=Laser Focus World|date=March 1, 2000}}</ref> and coherent control of atomic and molecular dynamics.

Bucksbaum helped to establish the new field of ultrafast x-ray science in early work at the [[Advanced Photon Source]] at [[Argonne National Laboratory]]<ref>{{cite news|last=Jacoby|first=Mitch|title=FAST SWITCH X-RAY|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/topstory/7944/7944notw7.html|newspaper=Chemical and Engineering News|date=2001-10-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Melville|first=Kate|title=Ultrafast X-ray Could Reveal Atoms In Motion|url=http://www.scienceagogo.com/news/20010925192429data_trunc_sys.shtml|access-date=2013-06-14|newspaper=Science A-Go-Go|date=2001-10-25}}</ref>
and most recently strong-field coherent x-ray-atom physics at x-ray [[free-electron laser]]s.

=== Professional service ===
Bucksbaum  served terms on the [[American Physical Society]] Executive Board, the [[Optical Society]] Board of Directors, and the [[National Academy of Sciences]] Board on Physics and Astronomy, as well as its Committee on AMO Science (CAMOS). He chaired its Decal Study in AMO Science, AMO 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=Important National Research Council Physics Report Released|url=http://www.aip.org/fyi/2006/105.html|access-date=2013-06-14|newspaper=FYI: The AIP Bulletin of Science Policy|date=2006-08-25}}</ref>  He has been a member of advisory committees for the [[United States Department of Energy|Department of Energy]] Division on Basic Energy Science (BESAC), [[NIST]] (Committee for Physics), The [[National Science Foundation]], and Science Advisory Committees for the Advanced Light Source at [[Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory|Berkeley National Lab]], the Advanced Photon Source at [[Argonne National Lab]], and the Linac Coherent Light Source at [[SLAC]] National Accelerator Lab. As of 2013 he was Chair of the Board on Physics and Astronomy of the National Academy.

He has served on the Editorial Board of ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'', and was the founding editor of the ''American Institute of Physics Virtual Journal of Ultrafast Science''.<ref>{{cite news |title=New Virtual Journal of Ultrafast Science now online |url=http://www.aip.org/press_release/ultrafast.html|access-date=2013-06-14|newspaper=AIP Press Release |date=June 7, 2002 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130601235950/http://www.aip.org/press_release/ultrafast.html|archive-date=2013-06-01}}</ref>
At Stanford and SLAC, he has served as Chair of the Photon Science faculty<ref name="Photon Science Chair">{{cite news|title=Report of the President to the Board of Trustees|url=http://news.stanford.edu/news/2007/july25/prezreport-072507.html|access-date=16 June 2013|newspaper=Stanford News|date=25 July 2007}}</ref> and Director of the Chemical Science Division.
